title: Spatial capture-recapture of spotted hyaena (Crocuta crocuta) from camera traps in Kasungu National Park, Malawi, annual surveys 2016 to 2018, with partial (single-flank) identities
creator: Davis, Robert Scott
citation: Davis, R. S. (2019). Spatial partial identity model for spatial capture-recapture analysis of large carnivores in Kasungu National Park, Malawi [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3540503
abstract: Daily camera-trap detections of individually identified spotted hyaena (Crocuta crocuta) in Kasungu National Park, Malawi, a miombo woodland, from three annual surveys (2016, 2017, 2018) of 90, 120 and 90 days at 17, 50 and 25 camera traps. Individuals were identified from pelage patterns; some are known from both flanks and some from one flank only, so a left-only and a right-only id may be the same animal (unit_identity; the authors fitted the two-flank spatial partial identity model). One row per individual x active trap-day; the deposited active-inactive matrix is the survey set. Sibling table for the other species of the same survey: davis_2019_kasungu_leopard_scr. Trap coordinates are centred on the array (local metres) because the leopard is IUCN Vulnerable.
samplingProtocol: Camera traps at trap stations in three annual surveys; each 24-hour day is an occasion and a binary matrix gives each trap's active days. Individuals identified from left and right flank pelage patterns; complete (two-flank) identities only where flanks were certainly from the same animal.
surveyEvidenceNote: tdf_<year>.csv gives each trap x day as active (1) or inactive (0); a trap-day is surveyed iff 1 (5990 trap-days). One leopard photograph (id 42, trap B20, 2017 day 16) falls on a day the matrix marks inactive; the photograph is believed and that trap-day is added to the survey set of both tables.
closureNote: each annual survey (period) treated as closed by the authors; open between years
geographicCoverage: Kasungu National Park, Malawi; trap array centre -13.1, 33.1 (0.1 degree); trap positions in __traps as local metres centred on the array
crs: local: metres, UTM 36S (EPSG:32736) easting/northing minus the mean trap position (processor-centred)

coordinatesCoarsened.method: trap coordinates centred on the array by the processor (local metres; exact UTM 36S positions withheld) because the leopard (IUCN VU) shares the camera array with the hyaena table; the array centre is given at 0.1 degree in geographicCoverage

designNote: Experimental list of E9: spatial capture-recapture with a trap key and __traps, three annual sessions as periods; partial identity (E2) in unit_identity. One species per table (ruling #20); the two tables share traps and survey set.
notes: unit_identity = the flanks from which the individual is known (both / left / right); single-flank ids may duplicate an animal known from the other flank. obs_side = the flank photographed on detection rows. Hyaenas were not sexed.

notShipped.scripts: process leopard.R / process hyaena.R: the authors' SPIM fitting code
notShipped.exact_coordinates: UTM 36S trap positions withheld (VU taxon on the array); __traps carries them centred on the array
